name: Surf
supports: Bensa machines were 1-player Italian copies of contemporary Gottlieb games; Bensa of Milan made or remanufactured machines 1973-1975
quote: Seems like in Italy in the 70s a few different companies started to copy a few of the name brand pinballs. Nearly an exact copy except all the Italy ones were 1 player not two our four player.

name: Jack in the box
supports: A Bensa 'Jack in the Box' was photographed and discussed; it has drop-down/lay-flat playfield targets
quote: That "Jack in the Box" looks very interesting, with the on the playfield drop down and lay flat targets ( kinda like InterFlip's Dragon) .

name: Jack in the box
supports: Reader comment on the source page corroborates a surviving example (same-site, so supporting color rather than an independent source)
quote: Buongiorno, ho ritrovato in una vecchia cantina un flipper Bensa tipo Jack in the box ( identico a quello che vedo nella vostra pagina).

name: Big Dryvers
supports: Pinside carries a separate Europlay-attributed Big Dryvers entry (dated 1979)
quote: Big Dryvers is a pinball machine from 1979, manufactured by Europlay.

name: Big Dryvers
supports: Pinside carries a separate Europlay-attributed Big Dryvers entry (dated 1979)
quote: Big Dryvers is a pinball machine from 1979, manufactured by Europlay.

name: Time Out
supports: Ripepi Time Out is a Far Out conversion
quote: This is an add-a-ball version of the 4-player Gottlieb's 1974 'Far Out' with similar artwork.

name: Hot Bullet
supports: artist signature dates it 1970
quote: The artist's signature and year in the lower right corner of the backglass indicates "Galli 70".

name: Arrow
supports: copy of Gottlieb Golden Arrow, maker Ripepi per cardholder
quote: A copy of Gottlieb's 1977 'Golden Arrow' with the backglass image reversed to show the warrior facing left. The manufacturer's name cannot be seen on the backglass or on the visible areas of the playfield but is printed on the cardholder.

name: Thrills
supports: Gottlieb parts, made in Italy, glass style dates ~1969
quote:
This game uses Gottlieb parts and reportedly was made in Italy.

The manufacture date of this game has not yet been identified to us, but the beaded backbox design was used by Gottlieb in 1969.

name: Lido
supports: unknown-maker wedgehead Lido matching an Italian kit profile
quote: Game has a wedgehead backbox with six score reels. No manufacturer name is apparent on the backglass, which shows patrons in a lounge setting with psychedelic art on the wall, being served by Playboy bunnies.

name: Neptune
supports: modification of Gottlieb's 1978 Neptune by Lodola
quote: A modification of Gottlieb's 1978 'Neptune'. This game has been seen with two scoring variations: six score reels and seven score reels, instead of Gottlieb's five.

name: El Viti
supports: kit for Gottlieb Harmony/Troubadour, Spanish bullfighting theme
quote: 5-digit score-reel scoring. This is a kit for Gottlieb's 1967 'Harmony' and Gottlieb's 1967 'Troubadour'. On the backglass, the Spanish word "TOROS" ("bulls") replaces the word "MUSIC".

name: Tex-Op
supports: version of Gottlieb Ten-Up on Gottlieb parts
quote: A version of Gottlieb's 1973 'Ten-Up'. Interestingly, the pinball machine was removed from the backglass bowling alley scene. Everything appears to be a reuse of Gottlieb parts except for the playfield and backglass which are not branded Gottlieb.

name: Sky Devil’s
supports: Italian game reusing Gottlieb Sky Dive art
quote: Game is located in Italy. The backglass and the cabinet artwork are the same as Gottlieb's 1974 'Sky Dive' which was an export to Italy.

name: The Royal
supports: copy of Gottlieb Royal Pair located in Italy
quote: A copy of Gottlieb's 1974 'Royal Pair'. The game pictured here was located in Italy.

name: Grand Slam
supports: Ice Show (Italy) conversion, LORI silkscreen
quote: This is a conversion of Gottlieb's 1966 'Ice Show (Italy)'. Reportedly, the backglass and playfield were silkscreened by LORI which, if so, then the art should be by Lorenzo Rimondini.

name: El Tigre
supports: 1-player SS version of Gottlieb Tiger
quote:
A 1-player SS version of Gottlieb's 1975 'Tiger' and shows a woman on the backglass instead of a man.

The lower left and right corners of the backglass indicate "Manufactured by El Tigre and Co."
This game is an example of Gottlieb Made In Italy.

name: The Circus Tiger
supports: copy of Gottlieb Tiger
quote: This is a copy of Gottlieb's 1975 'Tiger'.

name: New City
supports: Dama conversion of Williams Hot Line / Big Strike
quote: We had indicated that this game was a conversion kit for Williams' 1967 'Lunar Shot' but the backglass lamp placement and score reel placement along with the playfield layout look more like it is a conversion of Williams' 1966 'Hot Line' or its add-a-ball version Williams' 1966 'Big Strike'.

name: Mini Flipper
supports: IPDB attributes Mini Flipper to Rumatic, of Spain
quote: Rumatic, of Spain

name: Cosmos
supports: an unknown-manufacturer Cosmos exists in IPDB
quote: Cosmos — Unknown Manufacturer

name: Bowling
supports: Italian add-a-ball on Gottlieb parts; two glass variants known
quote: Reportedly, this game was made in Italy. It has the ball kick-up feature at the outhole and the five unmarked art elements on the backglass, typical of Italian add-a-ball games. It uses Gottlieb parts.

name: Big Sakem
supports: 1-player copy of Gottlieb Big Indian, attributed to Ripepi
quote: This is a 1-player copy of Gottlieb's 1974 'Big Indian'. We do not know if this is an add-a-ball game.

name: Big Sakem
supports: tilt.it credits Big Sakem to Nordamatic, presented at 3rd Enada
quote: 1974 Big Sakem (Nordmatic - presentato alla 3a Enada)

name: Lucky Man
supports: Museum of the Game also lists Lucky Man under Nordamatic (1976) — supports the Nordamatic attribution side of the conflict
quote: (not fetched; listing surfaced in search results as 'Lucky Man - Pinball by Nordamatic')

name: Pool Rabbit
supports: Existence, MM Computer Games backglass branding, Roger Rabbit-inspired art, ManilaMatic attribution, possible flipped Eight Ball layout
quote: The game is called "Pool Rabbit" by "MM Computer Games." Other forum members chimed in saying it was made by an Italian company called ManilaMatic in 1985, and the playfield is possibly a flipped "Eight Ball" layout.

name: Rugby
supports: Rugby by Sidam is a video pinball genre videogame, 1-2 alternating players
quote: A video pinball game. Rugby was produced by Sidam in 1976.

name: Rugby
supports: Rugby is Sidam's 1979 copy of Atari's Video Pinball
quote: Rugby | 1979 | Da Video Pinball (Atari)

name: Rugby
supports: Why it is named Rugby; a working unit survives; retheme of Atari Video Pinball
quote: Compared to Atari Video Pinball, ambientation changes completely, and then the background on which was reflected the image of the monitor. At the time, American football was almost unknown in Italy, and was identified as "a sort of Rugby football", hence probably the name.

name: Rugby
supports: Photo of a surviving unit, independently labeled a Video Pinball bootleg
quote: Level42 Rugby, Sidam Video Pinball bootleg !!!

name: Jungle Life
supports: Zaccaria's pre-production era of modifying and rebranding American pinballs (context for early copies like Jungle Life)
quote: Nel tardo 1967 si iniziò l'attività di modifica di flipper statunitensi, effettuando rebranding per i clienti locali.

name: Ten Up
supports: Claims Ten Up (EM, 1P, 1974) was Zaccaria's first model and a 4-player version followed in 1975
quote: la Zaccaria produsse il suo primo modello di flipper, il TEN UP modello elettromeccanico ad un solo giocatore

name: Queen Castle
supports: Confirms Queen's Castle as Zaccaria's sole 1978 electromechanical, 1 player
quote: Nel 1978 invece viene prodotto un solo modello elettromeccanico (lasciando piu' spazio alla produzione elettronica) il QUEEN'S CASTLE ad un giocatore

name: Soccer King
supports: Wikipedia's Zaccaria article uses Soccer Kings (plural) in its production-line photo caption
quote: Controllo produzione dei flipper Zaccaria Soccer Kings (1984 circa)
